messages:
alex.sales: Heads up 025-11-04 POC with ACME showing weird spend alerts. They say free credits didn't apply for a streaming chat test. Can we swarm?

sara.eng: pinging ops and billing. Do we have request IDs or timestamps?

alex.sales: acct id acct_9911. They started a streaming session at ~2025-11-04T03:12Z. No request ids from their side yet.

acme.poc: hi, we ran a demo script that streamed responses for a long conversation (~1.1M tokens over 6 hours). The console meter jumped and triggered an overage alert to our finance team. We thought trial credits would cover proof-of-concept.

nina.billing: streaming large sessions like that can burn through trial tokens quickly. By default streaming counts tokens as generated in near-real time; we issue trial credits at account creation but theres also a protection that blocks very long-running sessions from auto-applying credits if they exceed a threshold. I'll check the account's trial allocation.

leo.ops: I've pulled usage for acct_9911: between 2025-11-04T03:00 and 2025-11-04T09:00 there are 3 stream sessions recorded, totaling 1,112,400 generated tokens. Billing state shows TRIAL_ALLOCATED but an override flag STREAM_HIGH_USE = true (this prevents auto trial spend). Logs show a policy decision at 2025-11-04T03:14:22: override applied because session > 100k tokens.

sara.eng: override policy exists to prevent abuse, but for POCs we can make exceptions. Do we have an audit trail for the override? Why did it apply if trial was allocated?

leo.ops: policy is evaluated by the trial-guard lambda. It checked session_token_estimate > 100k and set flag. It also marks the usage as UNAPPLIED_TRIAL_PENDING until manual review.

nina.billing: standard ops: we don't auto-bill while pending, but alerts to the customer can still trigger if alert thresholds are in place. Did the POC receive a spend alert email?

acme.poc: yes, we got an email about potential overage. It was alarming for our finance lead. We paused after that. The email text said: "Your project exceeded 80% of the free credit allocation and may incur charges."

alex.sales: we should change language for POC accounts to avoid scaring customers. For this customer specifically can we do a manual review and either approve trial coverage or credit back?

nina.billing: we can approve coverage for this session. Need confirmation that this was an authorized POC run (sales attestation). Can you confirm, Alex?

alex.sales: I confirm ACME was running an authorized demo for ACME corp. They had sign-off from procurement to evaluate.

leo.ops: I'll flip the flag and reclassify the usage as APPLIED_TRIAL. That will remove the overage alert.

leo.ops: actioning now... done. Ledger reflects 0 USD charged and trial balance decremented by 1,112,400 tokens.

nina.billing: note: that will leave them with negative remaining trial balance (we allocated 1M tokens originally). We'll send a manual top-up of 200k tokens so they don't see negative numbers.

ops-bot: Manual trial top-up tx_20251104_9911 created for acct_9911 (200,000 tokens). State: PENDING.

nina.billing: top-up applied, ledger shows 200k credited. New visible balance: 87,600 tokens remaining.

acme.poc: thanks 1 That helps. Can we get a recommended pattern to avoid this in future?

sara.eng: For streaming demos use short-living sessions or summarize conversation periodically, and set a session id with idempotency for reconnects. Also recommend sampling streaming mode parameters (e.g., max_tokens_per_response) to cap. We'll add a sample demo script.

alex.sales: I'll send a note to ACME with guidance and update the sale POC checklist: include a pre-warn about the trial cap, and offer our demo environment (pre-budgeted).

acme.poc: appreciated. We'll re-run shorter tests.

nina.billing: I'll follow up w/ an internal doc to soften alert language for POC-class accounts.

alex.sales: ok closing this thread once the customer confirms their finance is OK. Thanks all.
